recipes.name: Fried Corn with Smoked Sausage
ingredients_raw: 1 pound smoked sausage, cut into 1-inch pieces

steps.text: Melt butter in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cook onion, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, and smoked sausage in butter until hot, 1 to 2 minutes.

Add corn to the skillet and reduce heat to medium; cover and cook until corn is tender, 5 to 7 minutes. Season with seasoned salt, garlic powder, onion powder, monosodium glutamate, and pepper; toss to combine. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Fried Corn with Smoked Sausage
raw_recipe.description: This delicious sausage fry recipe combines corn, onions, green and red bell peppers, and smoked sausage in a delicious one-pot meal.

review.reviewBody: I have made this dish lots of times and my family loves it. A key ingredient that is not listed is Lawry's Seasoned Pepper.(I use it instead of regular peppper) If you use it, I promise you will never go back to regular black pepper, I can hardly cook anything without it! Instead of chopping an onion I use a very large yellow sweet onion which I cut in thin strips. I cook it first for several minutes then add other ingredients. I have been buying the sausage that comes without any casing. I cut into very small pieces. I also use olive oil instead of butter.

I hate when people do this, but I'm going to review even though I made a few substitutions. I used fresh corn, which I know made a huge difference. It was sweet and lightly crisp in a way I know I couldn't have coaxed out of frozen corn. I also used fresh sausage, "country style" with sage seasoning, and that was tasty. Instead of full sized bell peppers, I used a bag of those multi-colored mini peppers, but I don't think that made a huge difference. Oh, and there was bacon involved. The fresh corn required a little different cooking technique. I started with chopped bacon and cooked it crisp to render the drippings, then removed the bacon, leaving the fat in the pan. I turned the heat way up and added the corn, left it in only enough to get a little char, maybe two minutes, and removed it to a bowl. I browned the cut-up sausage links until they were half-cooked and added the onions, peppers, and seasoning. I let those brown for a few minutes and then covered the pan and simmered until the sausage was fully cooked. Added the corn back to the pan and cooked just long enough to get it hot. Sprinkled the bacon over our individual servings. I had a few ears of corn left over from the other night and was looking for a way to use it up. We also enjoy the flavor of bacon with corn and peppers, and the fresh sausage was just personal preference. If you have sweet corn to use up, I hope this helps you use it here. I'm sure I'll make it in the winter with frozen corn, too.
Next time I would make the sausage pieces smaller and fry them first to get crispy edges

Thank you for the great recipe, David. I like the original and gave it five stars. I am adding these notes for my future use, not to "change" your recipe. 
I made it several times as written. Tonight, I turned it into a stir fry by using one can of corn, 1/2 cup chicken broth, two cups cooked white rice, 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (or more), 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp oregano, 1 tsp seasoned salt, 1 tsp onion powder, left out the garlic powder but added a garlic clove.

I have made this many times as written (well, w/o the msg) and it was great. Then lately I got a bit sassy w/ it and used part andouille sausage and part smoked sausage and added cajun seasoning as well. Yum. Gave it a bit of a kick. Last night, I made it ahead of time, put in crock pot on warm and went to son's bb game. Worked out well. Had more liquid than usual, but just dipped w/slotted spoon and it tasted the same. This is a great quick prep meal w/ ingredients that I always have in freezer.

I tried this recipe and everyone loved it. To be honest, I didn't follow the instructions explicitly, but used it as a springboard for my own spin on it. I used Cajun sausage and added Slap Ya Mama Cajun spice along with the spices listed. I also added 2 stalks of celery, chopped. I cut back on the corn -- using 1 can Southwest style corn (drained) and 1/2-cup frozen corn. I was prepared to add the whole 16 ounces of frozen corn, but stopped because I thought it had plenty of corn. I served over a bed of rice, sprinkled with cheddar cheese and add a dollop of sour cream. Yum! Thanks for the idea.

I made this exactly as indicated, INCLUDING the dreaded MSG (Goya Sazon)...it is excellent; and a great use of standard ingredients. As others have mentioned, it may have a bit to much watery liquid below its surface, just asking for straining the whole thing. Instead, I stirred-in a couple dollops of sour cream and a handful of shredded sharp cheddar cheese at end of cooking, which really pulled the whole thing together, both in body/texture and flavor (just my preference..stands on its own without the adds!)

Really good! the corn adds a nice sweetness to the dish. I hate to be "that guy" that posts reviews but then say I changed it... but I do add a little (tsp. to tbsp.) crushed red pepper for a little spice, and definitely omit the MSG. I also add a little soy sauce and water whisked with a little corn starch for a little bit of sauce. We usually serve over rice, also have done it over noodles. The whole family loves it, great base recipe, definitely in the dinner rotation! Thanks for the recipe :)

I was called upon to make a side dish on short notice. This recipe did the trick!! Everyone loved it and there was not a drop left. My niece even insisted on the recipe. 

I made a few changes:
Used spicy smoked beef sausage;
Omitted MSG, garlic and onion powder, used instead Lawry seasoned salt, Adobo light and black pepper;
Added yellow peppers.

I browned the sausage first, then added the veggies.

I'm already tasked with making this next month for the family gathering. Thanks for this recipe!
Easy to do and very tasty.. Only change I made was not adding the MSG..
I made this tonight for my husband and he loved it! Followed recipe as written minus the MSG and served over fried cheesy grits. A definite keeper for us.
It's very tasty as written. If you happen to have some some pimento cheese in the fridge, mix in some just before serving.
the only change I made was to serve this on hash brown. really good leftover too.

This was easy to make and full of flavor, even my picky kids liked it. I was surprised to see the recipe call for MSG, I don’t have any MSG not even sure what it looks like, so I substituted salt instead. I like that it’s high in protein and vegetables too. I browned the sausage first and removed the greasy fat before adding the veggies. Thank you for the recipe, will definitely make it again. 💚
Very good, tasty. I did add roma tomatoes in with the veggies and a little bit of salsa at the end. I served with potatoes with sour cream on top. It went good together.
I've made it many times before and it's a recipe to be kept.
My kids really enjoyed this recipe
Added rotel tomatoes and used canned corn. It was delicious.
Added one half cup cooked rice and additional seasoning.
I added some sliced fresh mushrooms and 3 chopped Roma tomatos to kick it up a notch.
